title: The Cepheid Bias: Resolving the Hubble Tension
description: The persistent 5-sigma discrepancy between the local distance ladder (H0 ~ 73.0 km/s/Mpc) and early-universe cosmological inference under flat LambdaCDM (H0 = 67.4 +/- 0.5 km/s/Mpc) represents a fundamental challenge in precision cosmology. This work demonstrates that this tension arises from an environment-dependent clock bias predicted by the Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP), wherein proper time is a dynamical scalar field that couples universally to non-gravitational matter and clocks. Because stellar pulsation rates operate in local proper time, calibrating classical Cepheids in deep-potential SN Ia host galaxies against diffuse, low-mass anchor galaxies systematically misestimates host distance moduli. This framework is tested using the complete public Riess et al. (2022; R22) sample of 37 distinct SN Ia host galaxies matched by exact supernova and PGC identifiers, with a homogeneous kinematic potential coordinate u_phi = V_rot / sqrt(2) derived from pinned HyperLEDA rotation velocities, RC3 diameters, and continuous environmental screening. Single-galaxy differential tests provide internal signatures with the sign predicted by TEP free from host-to-host peculiar velocity systematics: in M31, inner versus outer Cepheids exhibit an empirical Period-Luminosity offset of Delta W = +0.356 +/- 0.136 mag (2.6 sigma), increasing to +0.630 +/- 0.195 mag (3.24 sigma) under spatial PHAT matching, while OGLE-IV Cepheids in the LMC independently exhibit radial potential stratification at +0.0284 +/- 0.0086 mag (3.3 sigma). Across all 37 hosts, the generative endpoint likelihood yields Gamma_X = (1.156 +/- 0.958) x 10^7 km/s/Mpc (100% leave-one-host-out sign stability), with the cosmologically constrained expansion likelihood (Step 42) and joint multi-block framework (Step 44) consistently recovering the underlying cosmic expansion rate at H_app = 68.36 to 68.76 km/s/Mpc, in complete statistical concordance with Planck CMB cosmology.
